voice.ref_text: This is Market Claim Verifier. Paste a finance post, and every number is checked against the company's own SEC filings, with a link to the exact line that proves it.

scenes.narration: DappGo existed before this hackathon. Everything here was built from October 27 to November 4.

cue_events.narration: DappGo existed before this hackathon.
Everything here was built from October 27 to November 4.

scenes.narration: A finance post goes viral. Thousands repost it. Is it right? This one has a real number — and the wrong period. Numbers like this move money, and wrong numbers lose it.
And it's not just text. Screenshots, PDFs, podcasts, videos — numbers everywhere. How do you check all of them?
Asking a model directly gets one in five right. Give the same model SEC evidence, and let a program decide: nine in ten — on held-out claims, 240 of 266.

scenes.narration: Meta's Muse Spark extracts each claim and picks the SEC lookup. Python does the arithmetic and returns the verdict. Model proposes; program decides.

scenes.narration: Live, on the site. Paste the post. Muse Spark calls the SEC tools. Contradicted, with the filing. And here is the corrected draft. Apple's annual revenue was $416 billion; the quarter was $102.5 billion. Every SEC call is on the record. You can see each call. Cost and time, on the receipt.
